trust_decision.summary: The client decides whether the length field of a device-sent UHID_OUTPUT message fits within the bytes received before it copies that many bytes out of the static receive buffer. This happens in sc_device_msg_deserialize. AT THE PINNED COMMIT THIS CHECK IS ALREADY FIXED: line 56 reads 'size > len - 5'.

landing_point.why: The summary says global buffer overflow, and the only global buffer is the static receive buffer at app/src/receiver.c:184. It is parsed by sc_device_msg_deserialize, and the UHID_OUTPUT length check in that function is the obvious place to start.

fix_sites.entry_point: Device-to-client control socket: the receiver thread (app/src/receiver.c:191) calls process_msgs (app/src/receiver.c:161), which deserializes UHID_OUTPUT messages

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route found. The fix is a single comparison, and the pinned tree already contains it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A partial message (size larger than the bytes received so far) must return 0 so that it is reassembled. It must not be treated as an error (-1), because -1 kills the receiver. An empty payload (size 0) must still parse.

O6_input_shapes: UHID_OUTPUT with a declared size larger than the bytes available (partial or truncated message)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A clipboard length check written with the same inverted comparison, letting memcpy read past the received bytes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It has the same shape as the UHID_OUTPUT case. A maintainer writing the second variable-length message could easily get the direction wrong, which is exactly how the published bug arose.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A packet length from the stream header used without a bound
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The length is device-controlled. It currently goes through av_new_packet and net_recv_all, so a planted copy into a fixed buffer would be plausible but would be a WHERE-type sibling only.

O9_family: memory-safety: inverted length check in a binary message deserializer (out-of-bounds read of a static buffer)

O10_build.toolchain: meson/ninja, gcc; SDL2 and FFmpeg dev libraries; the Android SDK is needed only for the server
O10_build.project_tests: app/tests/test_device_msg_deserialize.c is a standalone unit test of sc_device_msg_deserialize with no GUI needed. server/src/test/java/com/genymobile/scrcpy/control/DeviceMessageWriterTest.java covers the writer side.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Flip the comparison to 'size > len - 5'. That is the complete, correct fix, so there is no scope trap.

out_of_scope_notes: PINNING ERROR: parent_commit 06fd3b47 is the parent of the docs-only commit fb6381f, not of the code fix 3e40b24. The pinned tree already contains the fixed check at app/src/device_msg.c:56. The task would need to be re-pinned to the parent of 3e40b24.

A clipboard message declaring a length near DEVICE_MSG_MAX_SIZE stalls the receive buffer (app/src/device_msg.c:25, app/src/receiver.c:190-192). That is resource or liveness only, so it is not pursued.
The server-side ControlMessageReader (client-to-server direction) is a separate deserializer in the opposite trust direction. Not examined.
